title: Kummer identifies curve cohomology with the Jacobian Tate module
statement:
Let $C_0/k_0$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve, put
$C=C_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and let $J$ be its
Jacobian, equipped with the canonical semilinear
$\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{k}_0/k_0)$-action of
[lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action]. For
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, the
Kummer twist gives natural
Galois-equivariant isomorphisms

$$
H^1(C,A_n(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}J[\ell^n](\overline{k}_0).
$$

Here $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and these isomorphisms are
compatible with the transition maps.
The Jacobian, Tate module, and twist in this display are those of
[def-sc-jacobian], [def-wf-abelian-tate-module], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

Here $\ell$ is prime and $n\geq1$. More explicitly, write
$\nu_C:C_{\mathrm{proet}}\to C_{\mathrm{et}}$ for
[def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The finite coefficient sheaf
$A_n(1)$ on $C_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is canonically
$\nu_C^*\mu_{\ell^n,C}$ by [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent]
with $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and uniformizer $\ell$.
The displayed $H^1$ can therefore be computed either on the pro-etale
site with this coefficient sheaf or on the etale site with
$\mu_{\ell^n,C}$, via [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison].
The transition on cohomology is induced by $z\mapsto z^\ell$, and the
transition on Jacobian torsion is $[\ell]$.
For $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(\overline{k}_0/k_0)$, the action on
cohomology is pullback along $t_\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{C_0}\times
\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ with the canonical comparison of roots-of-unity
sheaves; on $J(\overline{k}_0)$ it is precisely the point action specified
in [lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action].

proof.text: Put $K=\overline{k}_0$, $m=\ell^n$, and let $i_n:\mu_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,C}$ be the inclusion on the etale site. Specialize [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] to $F=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\varpi_F=\ell$, $A=A_n$, and annihilating exponent $r=n$. Its etale coefficient is $\mu_{m,C}\otimes_{A_n}A_n$, identified with $\mu_{m,C}$ by $u\otimes a\mapsto a u$ and inverse $u\mapsto u\otimes1$ (write the power action additively). Thus it gives the specified comparison $\nu_C^*\mu_{m,C}\cong A_n(1)$, commuting with scheme pullback and power transitions. By [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison], it suffices to construct the claimed maps on $H^1(C_{\mathrm{et}},\mu_{m,C})$. Both results apply since $\ell$ is invertible on $C$; neither assumes that $k_0$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 099W, lemma-compare-cohomology (1); finite Tate descent as in the cited node

proof.text:
The sequence $0\to\mu_{m,C}\xrightarrow{i_n}\mathbf G_{m,C}\xrightarrow{[m]}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to0$ is the Kummer sequence [def-sc-kummer-sequence], exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact]. Apply clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] to this short exact sequence with $u=\mathrm{id}_C$. It gives the exact segment
$$H^0(C,\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{[m]}H^0(C,\mathbf G_m)\longrightarrow H^1(C,\mu_m)\xrightarrow{H^1(i_n)}H^1(C,\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{H^1([m])}H^1(C,\mathbf G_m).$$
The $H^1$ arrow used here is induced by the inclusion, not a connecting map. Under [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic], $H^1(C,\mathbf G_m)$ is $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. The power endomorphism is the sum of $m$ copies of the identity in the abelian-sheaf category, so on the complexes computing cohomology it induces the sum of $m$ identity maps, and on Picard classes it is $[L]\mapsto[L^{\otimes m}]$.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; following long exact sequence in Section 03PK

proof.text: The geometric curve $C$ is smooth proper connected over the algebraically closed field $K$. By [lem-sc-global-functions], $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)=K$. By the units-sheaf definition [def-sc-gm-torsor] and degree-zero cohomology [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero], this identifies $H^0(C,\mathbf G_m)$ with $K^\times$. For $a\in K^\times$, the polynomial $X^m-a$ has a root $b\in K$; $b\ne0$ because $a\ne0$, so $[m]$ on $H^0$ is surjective. Exactness of Step 2 then says that $H^1(i_n)$ is injective and has image $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[m]$. Denote the resulting group isomorphism by $\beta_n:H^1(C,\mu_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(C)[m]$.

source.place: Section 03PK, long exact sequence after Lemma 03PL; blueprint proof paragraph 3

proof.text: The degree map of [def-sc-pic0] is a group homomorphism to $\mathbf Z$. If $L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C)[m]$, then $0=\deg(L^{\otimes m})=m\deg L$, whence $\deg L=0$ since $m>0$ and $\mathbf Z$ is torsion free. Conversely every $m$-torsion degree-zero class is $m$-torsion in $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$. Thus the inclusion identifies $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)[m]$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[m]$. Compose $\beta_n$ with the inverse of this inclusion and then the inverse of the point comparison $J(K)\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ of [lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action], restricted to $m$-torsion. This defines the required group isomorphism $\alpha_n:H^1(C,\mu_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}J[m](K)$. The comparison respects torsion because it is a group isomorphism. No primitive root or basis of either group is chosen.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, degree-zero argument and the representing comparison

proof.text:
Write $p_n:\mu_{\ell^{n+1}}\to\mu_{\ell^n}$ for $z\mapsto z^\ell$. The Kummer sequences at levels $n+1$ and $n$ have vertical maps $(p_n,[\ell],\mathrm{id})$ on their three terms. The first square commutes because $i_n(z^\ell)=i_{n+1}(z)^\ell$; the second commutes because $(x^\ell)^{\ell^n}=x^{\ell^{n+1}}$. Applying the cohomology functor [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] to the first square yields
$$H^1(i_n)\,H^1(p_n)=H^1([\ell])\,H^1(i_{n+1}).$$
As in Step 2, $H^1([\ell])$ is tensor power by $\ell$ on Picard classes. Since $\beta_n$ is the same inclusion map with its image restricted, this equality says $\beta_n(H^1(p_n)x)=\ell\beta_{n+1}(x)$. The point comparison of [lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action] commutes with multiplication by $\ell$. Restricting it to the degree-zero torsion groups therefore gives $\alpha_n(H^1(p_n)x)=[\ell]\alpha_{n+1}(x)$, exactly the transition compatibility asserted.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, compatibility of the finite-level identifications; the two Kummer squares written explicitly

proof.text: For $\sigma\in\Gamma=\operatorname{Aut}(K/k_0)$ set $s_\sigma=\operatorname{Spec}(\sigma)$ and $t_\sigma=\mathrm{id}_{C_0}\times s_\sigma$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], inverse image of $\mu_m$ along $t_\sigma$ is canonically $\mu_m$; on local units the comparison is pullback of functions. Pullback preserves the equation $z^m=1$ and the inclusion into units. Naturality in the sheaf map $i_n$, clause 3 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], therefore shows that $H^1(i_n)$ commutes with the induced actions on $H^1(C,\mu_m)$ and $H^1(C,\mathbf G_m)$. Under [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic-pullback], the latter action is $[L]\mapsto[t_\sigma^*L]$. Thus $\beta_n(\sigma x)=t_\sigma^*\beta_n(x)$. Restriction to degree-zero torsion and the equivariance of $J(K)\cong\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ in [lem-wf-geometric-jacobian-galois-action] give $\alpha_n(\sigma x)=\sigma\alpha_n(x)$. These are left actions: contravariance of Spec gives $t_{\sigma\tau}=t_\tau\circ t_\sigma$, and contravariance of pullback gives $t_{\sigma\tau}^*=t_\sigma^*t_\tau^*$; composition of cohomology pullback is clause 4 of the same functoriality node.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, Galois equivariance; Stacks Tags 01F8 and 040E for functoriality and Picard pullback

proof.text: Transport $\alpha_n$ back through the canonical coefficient and cohomology comparisons of Step 1. Their compatibility with scheme pullback and with power transitions preserves the equations of Steps 5 and 6. This gives the displayed natural Galois-equivariant isomorphisms with the coefficient $A_n(1)$ of the statement. Naturality here is the one furnished by the inclusion into the Picard group and the fixed representing comparison: a pullback of curves compatible with these data commutes with $i_n$ and with Picard pullback, so the same square in Step 6 commutes for that pullback. By [def-wf-abelian-tate-module], the transition $[\ell]$ on $J[\ell^n](K)$ is precisely its defining Tate-module system. The result asserts this compatible finite system; its proof requires no interchange of cohomology with an inverse limit.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, conclusion for the compatible finite system
